name: Turner Syndrome

prevalence.estimate: 1 in 2,000 to 1 in 2,500 live female births

criteria.description: Female phenotype with complete or partial absence of one X chromosome on karyotype analysis
Short stature (height <5th percentile or >2 SD below mean)
Primary ovarian insufficiency (elevated FSH, absent or delayed puberty)
Congenital heart defect (especially bicuspid aortic valve, coarctation of the aorta)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Karyotype showing 45,X or variant (mosaicism 45,X/46,XX; isochromosome Xq; ring X; partial X deletion) in a phenotypic female
diagnosticCriteria.notes: ~50% have classic 45,X; ~30% are mosaic; ~20% have structural X abnormalities. Prenatal diagnosis by amniocentesis or CVS is increasing. Phenotype varies widely, especially in mosaic cases.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Short stature in females with streak gonads
pathognomonic.notes: Average adult height ~147 cm (4'10") without GH treatment

common.symptomName: Primary ovarian insufficiency (absent or incomplete puberty)
Shield chest with widely spaced nipples

occasional.symptomName: Lymphedema of hands and feet (especially neonatal)
Recurrent otitis media and hearing loss

rare.notes: Leading cause of premature death in Turner syndrome; lifelong cardiovascular surveillance required

laboratory: Thyroid function tests (annual screening for hypothyroidism)
Fasting glucose and lipid panel (metabolic surveillance)
Liver function tests (elevated in some patients)
imaging: Echocardiography and cardiac MRI (bicuspid aortic valve, coarctation, aortic dilation)
Renal ultrasound (horseshoe kidney, duplicated collecting system)
Aortic imaging with MRI at regular intervals throughout life
genetic: Structural X abnormalities: isochromosome Xq, ring X, partial deletions (~20%)
SHOX gene haploinsufficiency accounts for short stature
Y chromosome material should be checked (risk of gonadoblastoma if present)
other: Neuropsychological assessment (nonverbal learning difficulties, visuospatial processing)

distinguishingFeatures: RAS-MAPK pathway gene mutations (PTPN11, RAF1, etc.)
Pulmonary stenosis more common than left-sided heart defects
Delayed bone age with catch-up growth

redFlags: Aortic root dilation requiring surgical intervention
Aortic dissection (medical emergency, especially in pregnancy)
Y chromosome material on karyotype (gonadoblastoma risk; prophylactic gonadectomy indicated)
Pregnancy (very high cardiovascular risk; requires specialized monitoring)
references: Gravholt CH, et al. Turner syndrome: mechanisms and management. Nat Rev Endocrinol. 2019;15(10):601-614.
Gravholt CH, et al. Clinical practice guidelines for the care of girls and women with Turner syndrome. Eur J Endocrinol. 2017;177(3):G1-G70.
Bondy CA, Turner Syndrome Study Group. Care of girls and women with Turner syndrome: a guideline of the Turner Syndrome Study Group. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2007;92(1):10-25.
Sybert VP, McCauley E. Turner's syndrome. N Engl J Med. 2004;351(12):1227-1238.
